text: 四万万人齐下泪，天涯何处是神州
pinyin: sì wàn wàn rén qí xià lèi, tiān yá hé chù shì shén zhōu
literal: four hundred million · people · together · shed · tears, world's end · where · is · the Divine Land
natural: four hundred million weep together; where in the world is China now?

meaning.en: Tan Sitong's cry of grief for a country in crisis: the whole nation weeps, and the homeland seems to have nowhere left to stand.
meaning.zh: 谭嗣同的悲愤之句：全国四万万人一同落泪，可祖国的山河究竟何在？

equivalents: the whole nation weeps
where is the homeland now?

examples.zh: 读到“四万万人齐下泪，天涯何处是神州”，课堂上一片寂静。
examples.en: When we read 'four hundred million weep together; where in the world is the Divine Land?', the classroom fell silent.

examples.zh: 纪念馆的展板上写着“四万万人齐下泪，天涯何处是神州”，讲的是甲午战败后的悲愤。
examples.en: A panel in the museum quotes 'four hundred million weep together; where in the world is the Divine Land?', speaking of the grief after the defeat of 1895.

story.en: Tan Sitong (1865-1898), a leader of the 1898 Reform Movement, wrote the poem after the humiliating treaty that ended the Sino-Japanese War: 'Nothing in the world can match this spring sorrow; I can only weep to the dark heavens.'
story.zh: 谭嗣同（1865—1898），戊戌变法的领袖之一，在甲午战败、签订屈辱条约后写下此诗：“世间无物抵春愁，合向苍冥一哭休。四万万人齐下泪，天涯何处是神州。”

usage.en: A quoted poem couplet, solemn and literary. 四万万 was the usual round figure for China's population in the late Qing; 神州 is a poetic name for China. Quoted when discussing the national crisis of the 1890s.
usage.zh: 引用的诗句，庄重、书面。“四万万”是晚清对全国人口的习惯说法，“神州”是中国的雅称。多在谈论19世纪90年代的民族危机时引用。

text: 吾至爱汝，即此爱汝一念，使吾勇于就死也
pinyin: wú zhì ài rǔ, jí cǐ ài rǔ yī niàn, shǐ wú yǒng yú jiù sǐ yě
literal: I · most · love · you, precisely · this · love · you · one thought, makes · me · brave · to · face · death
natural: because I love you so dearly, I dare to die

meaning.en: Lin Juemin to his wife on the eve of the 1911 uprising: it is the very love he bears her that gives him the courage to face death.
meaning.zh: 林觉民写给妻子的话：正因为深爱着你，才有勇气为理想赴死。

equivalents: my love for you gives me the courage to die
love made brave enough to die

examples.zh: 《与妻书》里有一句“吾至爱汝，即此爱汝一念，使吾勇于就死也”，读来令人落泪。
examples.en: The letter contains the line 'I love you most; it is this very love that makes me brave enough to die', which moves readers to tears.

examples.zh: 语文老师让大家背诵“吾至爱汝，即此爱汝一念，使吾勇于就死也”。
examples.en: The Chinese teacher asked everyone to memorise 'I love you most; it is this very love that makes me brave enough to die'.

story.en: Lin Juemin (1887-1911), a member of the Tongmenghui, wrote this farewell letter to his wife before the Guangzhou uprising of April 1911 and was executed after it failed; the letter, in classical Chinese, is one of the best-known of the age.
story.zh: 林觉民（1887—1911），同盟会会员，1911年4月广州起义前夕写下这封绝笔书给妻子，起义失败后就义；全信为文言，是那一时代最著名的书信之一。

usage.en: A quoted line in classical prose, solemn and literary; the letter is a school text. The letter is addressed to his wife Chen Yiying (意映) and was written in 1911 shortly before the Guangzhou uprising in which he died.
usage.zh: 引用的文言名句，庄重、书面，《与妻书》为中学课文。此信写给妻子陈意映，作于1911年广州起义前夕，林觉民在起义中牺牲。

text: 人能尽其才，地能尽其利，物能尽其用，货能畅其流
pinyin: rén néng jìn qí cái, dì néng jìn qí lì, wù néng jìn qí yòng, huò néng chàng qí liú
variants: 人尽其才，地尽其利，物尽其用，货畅其流
literal: people · can · exhaust · their · talent, land · can · exhaust · its · yield, things · can · exhaust · their · use, goods · can · flow · freely
natural: let people use their talents, land its yield, things their uses, and goods flow freely

meaning.en: Sun Yat-sen's four conditions for national wealth: every person fully employed, land fully productive, materials fully used, and goods moving freely.
meaning.zh: 孙中山提出的富强四要素：人才尽其所长，土地尽其所产，物资尽其所用，货物流通顺畅。

equivalents: the right person in the right job
make the most of people, land, resources and trade

examples.zh: 孙中山在《上李鸿章书》中写道：“人能尽其才，地能尽其利，物能尽其用，货能畅其流。”
examples.en: In his letter to Li Hongzhang, Sun Yat-sen wrote: 'Let people use their talents, land its yield, things their uses, and goods flow freely.'

examples.zh: 谈到经济建设，他引用了“人能尽其才，地能尽其利，物能尽其用，货能畅其流”。
examples.en: Speaking about economic development, he quoted 'let people use their talents, land its yield, things their uses, and goods flow freely'.

story.en: In 1894 the young Sun Yat-sen wrote to Li Hongzhang, arguing that the strength of Europe lay not only in warships and guns but in these four principles, 'the great rule of national wealth and strength'.
story.zh: 1894年，青年孙中山上书李鸿章，指出欧洲富强之本不尽在船坚炮利，而在这四件事，称之为“富强之大经，治国之大本”。

usage.en: Today it is usually quoted without 能 as 人尽其才，地尽其利，物尽其用，货畅其流 (listed as a variant); the original wording has 能 throughout. Quoted in talk of economic policy and the efficient use of resources.
usage.zh: 今天多引作不带“能”的形式：人尽其才，地尽其利，物尽其用，货畅其流（已列为异形）；原文每句都有“能”字。多用于谈经济政策和资源的有效利用。

text: 大学者，研究高深学问者也
pinyin: dà xué zhě, yán jiū gāo shēn xué wèn zhě yě
literal: university · is · the place · for · studying · advanced · learning · those · [particle]
natural: a university is a place for the pursuit of advanced learning

meaning.en: Cai Yuanpei's definition of a university: an institution for those who pursue advanced scholarship, not a stepping stone to office or wealth.
meaning.zh: 蔡元培对大学的定义：大学是研究高深学问的地方，不是升官发财的阶梯。

equivalents: a university is for the pursuit of advanced learning

examples.zh: 蔡元培在就职演说中说：“大学者，研究高深学问者也。”
examples.en: In his inaugural address Cai Yuanpei said: 'A university is a place for the pursuit of advanced learning.'

examples.zh: 校长开学典礼上重提“大学者，研究高深学问者也”，提醒新生不要只看文凭。
examples.en: At the opening ceremony the president recalled 'a university is a place for the pursuit of advanced learning', reminding freshmen not to care only about diplomas.

origin.source: 蔡元培北京大学就职演说（1917）

story.en: Cai Yuanpei (1868-1940) became president of Peking University in January 1917; in his inaugural speech he opened with this definition and urged students to study for learning's sake.
story.zh: 蔡元培（1868—1940）1917年1月就任北京大学校长，在就职演说中开宗明义提出这一定义，勉励学生为学问而求学。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of the purpose of higher education. Note the different line 大学者，非谓有大楼之谓也 (Mei Yiqi), which begins the same way.
usage.zh: 多在谈论高等教育宗旨时引用。注意与梅贻琦“大学者，非谓有大楼之谓也”开头相同但并非一句。

text: 自主的而非奴隶的，进步的而非保守的，进取的而非退隐的，世界的而非锁国的，实利的而非虚文的，科学的而非想象的
pinyin: zì zhǔ de ér fēi nú lì de, jìn bù de ér fēi bǎo shǒu de, jìn qǔ de ér fēi tuì yǐn de, shì jiè de ér fēi suǒ guó de, shí lì de ér fēi xū wén de, kē xué de ér fēi xiǎng xiàng de
literal: independent · not · slavish, progressive · not · conservative, enterprising · not · reclusive, global · not · closed-door, practical · not · empty-formal, scientific · not · imaginary
natural: independent not servile, progressive not conservative, enterprising not withdrawn, global not closed, practical not showy, scientific not fanciful

meaning.en: Chen Duxiu's six standards for youth in a new age, each set against its opposite.
meaning.zh: 陈独秀向青年提出的六条标准，每条都与其反面对举。

equivalents: six qualities of modern youth
a manifesto for the new youth

examples.zh: 《敬告青年》开篇提出：“自主的而非奴隶的，进步的而非保守的，进取的而非退隐的，世界的而非锁国的，实利的而非虚文的，科学的而非想象的。”
examples.en: 'Call to Youth' sets out: 'independent not servile, progressive not conservative, enterprising not withdrawn, global not closed, practical not showy, scientific not fanciful.'

examples.zh: 老师在讲新文化运动时，板书了“自主的而非奴隶的，进步的而非保守的，进取的而非退隐的，世界的而非锁国的，实利的而非虚文的，科学的而非想象的”。
examples.en: Teaching the New Culture Movement, the teacher wrote on the board: 'independent not servile, progressive not conservative, enterprising not withdrawn, global not closed, practical not showy, scientific not fanciful.'

story.en: Chen Duxiu (1879-1942) launched the magazine 《青年杂志》 (later 《新青年》) in 1915 with this essay, which lists six qualities he hoped young Chinese would have.
story.zh: 陈独秀（1879—1942）1915年创办《青年杂志》（后改名《新青年》），以此文发刊，列出他希望中国青年具备的六种品质。

usage.en: A long quoted passage, usually cited whole or by its first clause when discussing the New Culture Movement. Formal, written style.
usage.zh: 较长的引文，谈论新文化运动时整段或引前一两句。正式书面语。

text: 要拥护那德先生，便不得不反对孔教、礼法、贞节、旧伦理、旧政治
pinyin: yào yōng hù nà dé xiān shēng, biàn bù dé bù fǎn duì kǒng jiào, lǐ fǎ, zhēn jié, jiù lún lǐ, jiù zhèng zhì
literal: to · uphold · that · Mr. Democracy, then · cannot · but · oppose · Confucianism, ritual law, chastity, old ethics, old politics
natural: to uphold Mr Democracy one must oppose Confucianism, ritual codes, chastity, the old ethics and the old politics

meaning.en: Chen Duxiu's New Culture Movement argument: to defend democracy ('Mr De') China had to reject the old order, from Confucian teaching to traditional politics.
meaning.zh: 陈独秀在新文化运动中的论断：要维护民主（“德先生”），就必须反对从孔教到旧政治的一整套旧秩序。

equivalents: democracy requires breaking with the old order

examples.zh: 讲到五四运动，课本引用了“要拥护那德先生，便不得不反对孔教、礼法、贞节、旧伦理、旧政治”。
examples.en: On the May Fourth Movement the textbook quotes 'to uphold Mr Democracy one must oppose Confucianism, ritual codes, chastity, the old ethics and the old politics'.

examples.zh: 他在论文里分析了“要拥护那德先生，便不得不反对孔教、礼法、贞节、旧伦理、旧政治”的时代背景。
examples.en: His paper analyses the background to 'to uphold Mr Democracy one must oppose Confucianism, ritual codes, chastity, the old ethics and the old politics'.

origin.source: 陈独秀《本志罪案之答辩书》（《新青年》，1919年1月）

story.en: Replying to critics of 《新青年》, Chen Duxiu named 'Mr De' (Democracy) and 'Mr Sai' (Science) as the two remedies for China's ills and spelled out what upholding them meant opposing.
story.zh: 面对对《新青年》的攻击，陈独秀提出德先生（民主）与赛先生（科学）是救治中国的两剂药，并说明拥护它们就必须反对什么。

usage.en: Quoted as a statement of the iconoclastic strand of the May Fourth era (see 德先生和赛先生). Historical reference; later scholars debate how fairly it described Confucian tradition.
usage.zh: 作为五四时期反传统一派的代表性论述引用（参见“德先生和赛先生”）。属历史性引用；后来学者对它是否公允评价儒家传统多有讨论。

text: 尝试成功自古无，放翁这话未必是；我今为下一转语，自古成功在尝试
pinyin: cháng shì chéng gōng zì gǔ wú, fàng wēng zhè huà wèi bì shì, wǒ jīn wèi xià yī zhuǎn yǔ, zì gǔ chéng gōng zài cháng shì
literal: trying · success · since · antiquity · none, Fangweng · this · saying · not necessarily · right, I · now · give · one · turning · word, since · antiquity · success · lies in · trying
natural: 'No success comes from trying', says Lu You, but I say the opposite: success has always come from trying

meaning.en: Hu Shih turns an old line on its head: success has never come without experiment, so one should be bold enough to try.
meaning.zh: 胡适把古人的话反过来说：成功都是从尝试中来的，所以要敢于尝试。

equivalents: nothing ventured, nothing gained
you never know until you try

examples.zh: 他把“尝试成功自古无，放翁这话未必是；我今为下一转语，自古成功在尝试”抄在笔记本扉页，作为座右铭。
examples.en: He copied 'No success comes from trying, says Fangweng; I doubt it. Let me turn it round: success has always come from trying' on the flyleaf of his notebook as a motto.

examples.zh: 胡适《尝试篇》写道：“尝试成功自古无，放翁这话未必是；我今为下一转语，自古成功在尝试。”
examples.en: Hu Shih's 'On Trying' says: 'No success comes from trying, says Fangweng; I doubt it. Let me turn it round: success has always come from trying.'

story.en: Hu Shih (1891-1962), pioneer of vernacular Chinese poetry, published 《尝试集》 (Experiments) in 1920, the first collection of new-style poems; its title poem 《尝试篇》 contains this couplet.
story.zh: 胡适（1891—1962），白话新诗的开创者，1920年出版第一部白话新诗集《尝试集》，集中《尝试篇》即含此句。

usage.en: Often quoted in short as 自古成功在尝试 to encourage experiment. 放翁 is Lu You (陆游), whose line 'no success comes from trying' Hu Shih answers.
usage.zh: 常单引末句“自古成功在尝试”以鼓励尝试。放翁即陆游，胡适是在回应其“尝试成功自古无”之说。

text: 醉过才知酒浓，爱过才知情重
pinyin: zuì guò cái zhī jiǔ nóng, ài guò cái zhī qíng zhòng
literal: drunk · past · only then · know · wine · strong, loved · past · only then · know · feeling · heavy
natural: only after being drunk do you know how strong wine is; only after loving do you know how deep feeling runs

meaning.en: Some things can only be understood by experiencing them: you learn the strength of wine by getting drunk, and the weight of love by loving.
meaning.zh: 有些事只有亲身经历才懂：醉过才知酒的浓，爱过才知情的深。

equivalents: you only know once you've been there
love teaches what words cannot

examples.zh: 分手以后，他才懂得“醉过才知酒浓，爱过才知情重”。
examples.en: After the break-up he understood that 'only after being drunk do you know how strong wine is; only after loving, how deep feeling runs'.

examples.zh: 歌词里那句“醉过才知酒浓，爱过才知情重”被很多人当作签名。
examples.en: Many people use the lyric 'only after being drunk do you know how strong wine is; only after loving, how deep feeling runs' as their personal tagline.

story.en: In the new-style poem 《梦与诗》 Hu Shih says that dreams are made of ordinary experience and ends: 'Only after being drunk do you know how strong wine is; only after loving, how deep feeling runs.'
story.zh: 胡适在白话诗《梦与诗》中写梦由平常经验变幻而成，诗中有“醉过才知酒浓，爱过才知情重”。

usage.en: Commonly quoted about love and experience. Usually credited to Hu Shih's poem 《梦与诗》 (1920), where it is followed by 我不能做你的诗，你也不能做我的梦.
usage.zh: 常用于谈爱情与阅历。一般认为出自胡适《梦与诗》（1920），其后是“我不能做你的诗，你也不能做我的梦”。

text: 词人者，不失其赤子之心者也
pinyin: cí rén zhě, bù shī qí chì zǐ zhī xīn zhě yě
literal: ci-poet · is · one · not · lose · his · newborn child's · heart · one · [particle]
natural: a ci poet is one who has never lost a child's heart

meaning.en: Wang Guowei on what makes a ci poet: someone who keeps the innocence and sincerity of a child.
meaning.zh: 王国维论词人：真正的词人是不失去赤子般纯真之心的人。

equivalents: a poet is a child at heart

examples.zh: 王国维说“词人者，不失其赤子之心者也”，用来评价李煜。
examples.en: Wang Guowei said 'a ci poet is one who has never lost a child's heart', in praise of Li Yu.

examples.zh: 讲座以“词人者，不失其赤子之心者也”开头，谈诗人的真诚。
examples.en: The lecture began with 'a ci poet is one who has never lost a child's heart' and went on to poets' sincerity.

story.en: Wang Guowei (1877-1927) wrote this in 《人间词话》 (1908), praising Li Yu, the last ruler of the Southern Tang: though raised in the palace, he never lost his sincerity.
story.zh: 王国维（1877—1927）在《人间词话》（1908）中评南唐后主李煜，说他生于深宫而不失真诚，故为词人。

usage.en: A literary-criticism line, formal; the original remark is about Li Yu (后主). See also 赤子之心.
usage.zh: 文学批评名句，较正式；原文评李煜（后主）。参见“赤子之心”。

text: 脱心志于俗谛之桎梏
pinyin: tuō xīn zhì yú sú dì zhī zhì gù
literal: free · mind and will · from · conventional wisdom · 's · shackles
natural: free the mind from the shackles of received opinion

meaning.en: Chen Yinke on the purpose of scholarship: to release the mind from the fetters of conventional opinion so that truth may come to light.
meaning.zh: 陈寅恪论读书治学的目的：使心志摆脱世俗成见的束缚，真理才能得到发扬。

equivalents: free the mind from received opinion
break the shackles of convention

examples.zh: 他把“脱心志于俗谛之桎梏”刻在书房里，提醒自己做学问不可人云亦云。
examples.en: He kept 'free the mind from the shackles of received opinion' in his study to remind himself not to follow the crowd.

examples.zh: 毕业赠言里有一句“脱心志于俗谛之桎梏”。
examples.en: One graduation message read 'free the mind from the shackles of received opinion'.

origin.source: 陈寅恪《海宁王静安先生纪念碑铭》（1929）

story.en: Chen Yinke (1890-1969) wrote the inscription for the memorial to Wang Guowei at Tsinghua in 1929: 'The scholar reads to free the mind from the shackles of conventional truths, so that truth may flourish.'
story.zh: 陈寅恪（1890—1969）1929年为清华园王国维纪念碑撰铭，序中云：“士之读书治学，盖将以脱心志于俗谛之桎梏，真理因得以发扬。”

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of academic independence; usually together with the next line, 思想而不自由，毋宁死耳. Literary.
usage.zh: 谈学术独立时引用，常与下句“思想而不自由，毋宁死耳”连用。书面语。

text: 思想而不自由，毋宁死耳
pinyin: sī xiǎng ér bù zì yóu, wú nìng sǐ ěr
literal: thought · yet · not · free, better · die · [particle]
natural: if thought is not free, one might as well die

meaning.en: Chen Yinke's declaration that without freedom of thought life is not worth living.
meaning.zh: 陈寅恪的名言：思想若不自由，不如死去。

equivalents: give me freedom of thought or give me death

examples.zh: 他在演讲结尾说：“思想而不自由，毋宁死耳。”
examples.en: He ended the speech with 'if thought is not free, one might as well die'.

examples.zh: 很多学人把“思想而不自由，毋宁死耳”视为学术信条。
examples.en: Many scholars treat 'if thought is not free, one might as well die' as an academic creed.

origin.source: 陈寅恪《海宁王静安先生纪念碑铭》（1929）

story.en: The line comes in the preface to the inscription written by Chen Yinke in memory of Wang Guowei: 'If thought is not free, better to die; this is the meaning for which the sages of all ages have given their lives.'
story.zh: 此句见陈寅恪为纪念王国维所撰碑铭之序：“思想而不自由，毋宁死耳。斯古今仁圣所同殉之精义。”

usage.en: Literary and emphatic; quoted in discussions of academic freedom. Follows 脱心志于俗谛之桎梏 in the original.
usage.zh: 书面、语气强烈，谈学术自由时引用。原文紧接在“脱心志于俗谛之桎梏”之后。

text: 忍看朋辈成新鬼，怒向刀丛觅小诗
pinyin: rěn kàn péng bèi chéng xīn guǐ, nù xiàng dāo cóng mì xiǎo shī
literal: bear · to see · friends · become · new · ghosts, angrily · toward · forest of blades · seek · little · poem
natural: how can I bear to watch friends become new ghosts; in anger I seek a poem amid the blades

meaning.en: Lu Xun's couplet of grief and defiance: friends are being killed, and he answers by writing poetry in the face of the blades.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅的悲愤之句：眼看朋友相继被杀，他在刀丛之中愤而作诗。

equivalents: writing poems in the face of the blades
grief turned into defiance

examples.zh: 鲁迅写“忍看朋辈成新鬼，怒向刀丛觅小诗”，是为悼念被害的青年作家。
examples.en: Lu Xun wrote 'how can I bear to watch friends become new ghosts; in anger I seek a poem amid the blades' in mourning for murdered young writers.

examples.zh: 展览中展出了手稿，上面是“忍看朋辈成新鬼，怒向刀丛觅小诗”。
examples.en: The exhibition showed the manuscript bearing 'how can I bear to watch friends become new ghosts; in anger I seek a poem amid the blades'.

origin.source: 鲁迅《无题》（“惯于长夜过春时”，1931年）

story.en: Lu Xun wrote this untitled regulated poem in 1931 after the execution of young left-wing writers, among them the 'Five Martyrs'; the full poem begins 惯于长夜过春时.
story.zh: 1931年左联五位青年作家被害后，鲁迅写下这首无题律诗，全诗首句为“惯于长夜过春时”。

usage.en: Quoted when discussing Lu Xun's response to the repression of the early 1930s, and more broadly writing as resistance. Solemn and literary.
usage.zh: 谈论鲁迅对1930年代初白色恐怖的态度，或以写作作抗争时引用。庄重、书面。

text: 两间余一卒，荷戟独彷徨
pinyin: liǎng jiān yú yī zú, hè jǐ dú páng huáng
literal: between · heaven and earth · left · one · soldier, shouldering · halberd · alone · wandering
natural: one soldier left between heaven and earth, halberd on shoulder, wandering alone

meaning.en: Lu Xun's self-portrait as a lone fighter: the camp has dispersed, and he still carries his weapon, uncertain which way to go.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅的自画像：同伴星散，只剩他一个战士，扛着戟，孤独徘徊。

equivalents: a lone soldier with no army left
fighting on alone

examples.zh: 评论家常用“两间余一卒，荷戟独彷徨”来形容鲁迅五四之后的心境。
examples.en: Critics often use 'one soldier left between heaven and earth, halberd on shoulder, wandering alone' to describe Lu Xun's mood after May Fourth.

examples.zh: 书的扉页上印着“两间余一卒，荷戟独彷徨”。
examples.en: The flyleaf of the book is printed with 'one soldier left between heaven and earth, halberd on shoulder, wandering alone'.

story.en: In 1933 Lu Xun wrote this poem on a copy of his story collection 《彷徨》: 'In the new literary garden, quiet; on the old battlefield, peace. Between heaven and earth, one soldier left, halberd on shoulder, wandering alone.'
story.zh: 1933年鲁迅在小说集《彷徨》上题诗：“寂寞新文苑，平安旧战场。两间余一卒，荷戟独彷徨。”

usage.en: Quoted for loneliness in a struggle. 彷徨 echoes the title of his 1926 story collection 《彷徨》. Literary.
usage.zh: 用来形容斗争中的孤独。“彷徨”呼应其1926年小说集《彷徨》的书名。书面语。

text: 运交华盖欲何求，未敢翻身已碰头；破帽遮颜过闹市，漏船载酒泛中流
pinyin: yùn jiāo huá gài yù hé qiú, wèi gǎn fān shēn yǐ pèng tóu, pò mào zhē yán guò nào shì, lòu chuán zài jiǔ fàn zhōng liú
literal: luck · meets · canopy star · want · what · seek, not yet · dare · turn over · already · bump · head, ragged · hat · cover · face · pass · busy market, leaky · boat · carry · wine · float · mid-stream
natural: with luck under the Canopy star what can I seek? Before I dare turn over I have hit my head; in a battered hat I cross the busy market, in a leaky boat with wine I drift midstream

meaning.en: Lu Xun's wry verse on bad luck: whatever he tries, he bumps his head; he crosses the market in a ragged hat and drifts on in a leaky boat.
meaning.zh: 鲁迅自嘲运气不佳：什么也没做就碰了头，戴着破帽走过闹市，坐着漏船载酒漂在江中。

equivalents: bad luck at every turn
dogged by misfortune

examples.zh: 他倒霉透顶，朋友笑说：“运交华盖欲何求，未敢翻身已碰头；破帽遮颜过闹市，漏船载酒泛中流。”
examples.en: He was thoroughly unlucky, and a friend joked: 'With luck under the Canopy star what can I seek? Before I dare turn over I have hit my head; in a battered hat I cross the busy market, in a leaky boat with wine I drift midstream.'

examples.zh: 课堂上分析了“运交华盖欲何求，未敢翻身已碰头；破帽遮颜过闹市，漏船载酒泛中流”中的自嘲笔法。
examples.en: The class analysed the self-mockery in 'With luck under the Canopy star what can I seek? Before I dare turn over I have hit my head; in a battered hat I cross the busy market, in a leaky boat with wine I drift midstream'.

story.en: Lu Xun wrote 《自嘲》 in October 1932; its next couplet is the famous 横眉冷对千夫指，俯首甘为孺子牛.
story.zh: 鲁迅1932年10月作《自嘲》，其后两句即名句“横眉冷对千夫指，俯首甘为孺子牛”。

usage.en: 华盖 is an unlucky star in fortune-telling, and Lu Xun's essay collection 《华盖集》 takes its name from it. The first couplet is often quoted alone for a run of bad luck; humorous and self-mocking.
usage.zh: “华盖”是命相中的凶星，鲁迅杂文集《华盖集》即以此得名。前两句常单独引用，形容接连倒霉；带自嘲和幽默。

text: 绝望之为虚妄，正与希望相同
pinyin: jué wàng zhī wéi xū wàng, zhèng yǔ xī wàng xiāng tóng
literal: despair · being · illusory, exactly · as · hope · same
natural: despair is as illusory as hope

meaning.en: Despair is no more real than hope: neither tells you what will happen, so one has no reason to give up.
meaning.zh: 绝望和希望一样都是虚幻的，谁也无法由此断定未来，因此没有理由放弃。

equivalents: despair is just as empty as hope

examples.zh: 鲁迅借用裴多菲的话：“绝望之为虚妄，正与希望相同。”
examples.en: Lu Xun borrowed Petőfi's words: 'despair is as illusory as hope'.

examples.zh: 心情低落时，她想起了“绝望之为虚妄，正与希望相同”。
examples.en: In low spirits she recalled 'despair is as illusory as hope'.

story.en: In the prose poem 《希望》 (1925), Lu Xun cites Petőfi: 'Despair is as illusory as hope.'
story.zh: 1925年散文诗《希望》中，鲁迅引裴多菲之语：“绝望之为虚妄，正与希望相同。”

usage.en: Lu Xun quotes this in 《希望》 as words of the Hungarian poet Sándor Petőfi (裴多菲) from a letter. Quoted in talk of pessimism and perseverance; literary.
usage.zh: 鲁迅在《希望》中引作匈牙利诗人裴多菲书信中的话。谈论悲观与坚持时引用，书面语。

text: 有一分热，发一分光
pinyin: yǒu yī fēn rè, fā yī fēn guāng
literal: have · one · portion · heat, give off · one · portion · light
natural: give as much light as you have heat

meaning.en: However small one's means, do what one can: shed as much light as one has warmth, like a firefly, without waiting for a torch.
meaning.zh: 条件有限也要尽力而为：有多少热就发多少光，不必等待火炬。

equivalents: do what you can with what you have
every little helps

examples.zh: 志愿者说：“有一分热，发一分光。”
examples.en: The volunteer said: 'If you have a little heat, give a little light.'

examples.zh: 校训里写着“有一分热，发一分光”，鼓励学生量力而为、服务社会。
examples.en: The school motto reads 'give as much light as you have heat', urging students to serve society as they can.

origin.source: 鲁迅《热风·随感录四十一》（1919）

story.en: Lu Xun urged young people to shed the cold cynicism of the age: 'If there is no torch, I will be the only light. If you have a little heat, give a little light, even as small as a firefly's.'
story.zh: 鲁迅劝青年摆脱冷气：“此后如竟没有炬火：我便是唯一的光。倘若有一分热，发一分光，就令萤火一般，也可以在黑暗里发一点光。”

usage.en: Often quoted in speeches, mottos and volunteer slogans; positive and neutral in register. The line is from the passage 倘若有一分热，发一分光，就令萤火一般，也可以在黑暗里发一点光.
usage.zh: 常见于演讲、格言和志愿服务口号，褒义。原文为“倘若有一分热，发一分光，就令萤火一般，也可以在黑暗里发一点光”。

text: 从来如此，便对么？
pinyin: cóng lái rú cǐ, biàn duì ma
literal: always · so · then · right · [question]
natural: it has always been so; does that make it right?

meaning.en: A challenge to tradition: the fact that something has always been done does not make it right.
meaning.zh: 对传统的质问：一向如此，并不等于正确。

equivalents: just because it's always been done doesn't make it right
tradition is no justification

examples.zh: 面对陈规旧习，他反问：“从来如此，便对么？”
examples.en: Faced with the old rules, he asked: 'It has always been so; does that make it right?'

examples.zh: 会上有人说一直都这样做，年轻人问：“从来如此，便对么？”
examples.en: When someone said it had always been done this way, the young man asked: 'It has always been so; does that make it right?'

story.en: In Lu Xun's first modern short story, the 'madman' narrator reflects on a world that eats people and asks: 'It has always been so; does that make it right?'
story.zh: 在鲁迅第一篇现代白话小说中，“狂人”思考这个吃人的世界，发问：“从来如此，便对么？”

usage.en: Said by the narrator in 《狂人日记》 (1918). Used to challenge habit and convention, often rhetorically; the narrator is the 'madman' of the story, not Lu Xun speaking in his own voice.
usage.zh: 出自《狂人日记》（1918）中狂人的话，用于质疑习惯和成规，多作反问。说话人是小说中的“狂人”，并非鲁迅本人口吻。

text: 我真傻，真的
pinyin: wǒ zhēn shǎ, zhēn de
literal: I · really · foolish, truly
natural: I was so stupid, truly

meaning.en: Xianglin's Wife's refrain of self-reproach: she blames her own foolishness for the loss of her child.
meaning.zh: 祥林嫂反复说的自责话：她把孩子被狼叼走归咎于自己的愚蠢。

equivalents: how foolish I was
if only I had known

examples.zh: 她望着空荡荡的屋子，喃喃自语：“我真傻，真的。”
examples.en: Looking at the empty house, she murmured: 'I was so stupid, truly.'

examples.zh: 读《祝福》时，最让学生难忘的是祥林嫂那句“我真傻，真的”。
examples.en: Reading 'New Year's Sacrifice', what students remember most is Xianglin's Wife's 'I was so stupid, truly'.

story.en: In 《祝福》 Xianglin's Wife tells everyone how her son Ah Mao was taken by a wolf; she says again and again: 'I was so stupid, truly. I only knew that wolves come down to the village when they have nothing to eat in the mountains in snow.'
story.zh: 《祝福》中祥林嫂向人讲述儿子阿毛被狼叼走，一再说：“我真傻，真的。我单知道雪天是野兽在深山里没有食吃，才会到村庄里来。”

usage.en: A character's line from 《祝福》 (1924), spoken by Xianglin's Wife and not by Lu Xun himself. Quoted for self-reproach and sympathy for a ruined life; sometimes used playfully today. Casual, spoken register.
usage.zh: 出自《祝福》（1924）祥林嫂之口，并非鲁迅本人所说。多用于自责，或表达对不幸者的同情；今天有时也半开玩笑地引用。口语。

text: 这个人也许永远不回来了，也许“明天”回来
pinyin: zhè gè rén yě xǔ yǒng yuǎn bù huí lái le, yě xǔ míng tiān huí lái
literal: this · person · perhaps · forever · not · come back, perhaps · tomorrow · come back
natural: this man may never come back, or he may come back tomorrow

meaning.en: The closing line of Shen Congwen's 'Border Town': the young man may be gone for ever, or may return tomorrow; the story ends in open-ended longing.
meaning.zh: 沈从文《边城》结尾：那个人也许一去不回，也许明天就回来；小说在未知的等待中收束。

equivalents: he may never return, or he may be back tomorrow

examples.zh: 评论《边城》的文章常引用最后一句：“这个人也许永远不回来了，也许“明天”回来。”
examples.en: Essays on 'Border Town' often quote its last line: 'This man may never come back, or he may come back “tomorrow”.'

examples.zh: 故事就停在“这个人也许永远不回来了，也许“明天”回来”，留给读者无限想象。
examples.en: The story stops at 'this man may never come back, or he may come back “tomorrow”', leaving readers to imagine.

story.en: Shen Congwen's novella 《边城》 (1934) tells of Cuicui, a boatman's granddaughter in western Hunan; it ends with her waiting for Nuosong, who has left and may not return.
story.zh: 沈从文中篇小说《边城》（1934）讲湘西撑船人的孙女翠翠，结尾她仍在等待离去的傩送，不知他是否回来。

usage.en: Quoted when discussing 《边城》 or open endings and quiet longing. In the original 明天 is in quotation marks. Literary.
usage.zh: 谈论《边城》、开放式结尾和淡淡的怅惘时引用。原文“明天”带引号。书面语。

text: 你们杀死了一个李公朴，会有千百万个李公朴站起来
pinyin: nǐ men shā sǐ le yī gè lǐ gōng pǔ, huì yǒu qiān bǎi wàn gè lǐ gōng pǔ zhàn qǐ lái
literal: you · kill · [past] · one · Li Gongpu, will · have · thousands · millions · Li Gongpu · stand · up
natural: you have killed one Li Gongpu, but millions of Li Gongpus will stand up

meaning.en: Wen Yiduo's defiant words to the assassins of Li Gongpu: killing one person cannot silence a cause.
meaning.zh: 闻一多对杀害李公朴者的怒斥：杀死一个人，压不住千百万人的声音。

equivalents: you can kill one man but not the cause
martyrs breed more

examples.zh: 演讲者高声说：“你们杀死了一个李公朴，会有千百万个李公朴站起来！”
examples.en: The speaker cried out: 'You have killed one Li Gongpu, but millions of Li Gongpus will stand up!'

examples.zh: 纪念会上有人引用“你们杀死了一个李公朴，会有千百万个李公朴站起来”。
examples.en: At the memorial meeting someone quoted 'you have killed one Li Gongpu, but millions of Li Gongpus will stand up'.

story.en: On 15 July 1946 in Kunming, at the memorial meeting for the murdered democrat Li Gongpu, Wen Yiduo (1899-1946) gave his last speech; he was shot dead that afternoon.
story.zh: 1946年7月15日，闻一多（1899—1946）在昆明李公朴先生追悼会上作最后一次演讲，当天下午遇害。

usage.en: Used as a historical quotation or as a slogan about the unstoppable spread of a cause; solemn. Wen Yiduo spoke these words in July 1946 and was himself killed hours later.
usage.zh: 作为历史引文，或用来说明一种事业无法被扼杀；庄重。闻一多1946年7月说此话，数小时后遇害。

text: 那河畔的金柳，是夕阳中的新娘；波光里的艳影，在我的心头荡漾
pinyin: nà hé pàn de jīn liǔ, shì xī yáng zhōng de xīn niáng, bō guāng lǐ de yàn yǐng, zài wǒ de xīn tóu dàng yàng
literal: that · riverbank · 's · golden willow, is · sunset · in · 's · bride, ripples · in · 's · bright · reflection, in · my · 's · heart · ripple
natural: the golden willows by the river are brides in the setting sun; their bright reflections ripple in my heart

meaning.en: Xu Zhimo's picture of the Cam at dusk: the willows glow like brides in the sunset and their reflections in the water stir his heart.
meaning.zh: 徐志摩笔下的康河黄昏：金色的柳树像夕阳中的新娘，水中的倒影在心头荡漾。

equivalents: willows as brides in the sunset

examples.zh: 教室里，学生齐声朗读“那河畔的金柳，是夕阳中的新娘；波光里的艳影，在我的心头荡漾”。
examples.en: In the classroom the students read aloud together 'the golden willows by the river are brides in the setting sun; their bright reflections ripple in my heart'.

examples.zh: 明信片上印着“那河畔的金柳，是夕阳中的新娘；波光里的艳影，在我的心头荡漾”和一幅剑桥的风景。
examples.en: The postcard carries 'the golden willows by the river are brides in the setting sun; their bright reflections ripple in my heart' beside a view of Cambridge.

story.en: Xu Zhimo (1897-1931) wrote 《再别康桥》 in November 1928 on his last visit to Cambridge, where he had studied; the poem is among the best-known in modern Chinese.
story.zh: 徐志摩（1897—1931）1928年11月重访曾就读的剑桥，作《再别康桥》，为现代汉语诗歌中最著名的作品之一。

usage.en: Quoted when describing evening scenery or when talking about Cambridge; poetic and romantic. 康桥 is Xu Zhimo's name for Cambridge.
usage.zh: 描写黄昏景色或谈及剑桥时引用，诗意浪漫。“康桥”是徐志摩对剑桥的译名。
